transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because I'm having a serious problem with bridges. 

The moment I realize a bridge crossing is unavoidable, my heart just starts pounding. My hands get all damp on the steering wheel—or the armrest if someone else is driving—and I get this terrible rush of fear before I’m even on the bridge itself. It's very intense, and I just can't keep dealing with it on my own anymore.
Do you experience this same intense fear in other situations, such as being in crowds, standing in line, or using public transportation?

No, I don't. It's really just... well, just the bridges. I don't have any trouble being in crowds or standing in line at the store. And public transportation is fine. I don't get that pounding heart or anything on a bus or a train. It's strictly when I have to cross a bridge.

latest_inference.note: The patient explicitly denies fear in crowds, lines, or public transportation, which effectively rules out Agoraphobia (F40.00, F40.01). The symptoms are specific to bridges, confirming a Specific Phobia (situational type).
